questions.q:
With reference to India's fiscal framework as reflected in the Union Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. The debt-to-GDP ratio has replaced the fiscal deficit ratio as the primary target.
2. The new target level is lower than the 40 per cent level associated with the FRBM framework.
3. Fiscal space under the new rule makes the FY27 deficit reduction milder than the cuts of FY22 to FY26.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the comparison: a target near 50 per cent is higher than the 40 per cent level, so the rule permits a larger sustained debt. Since present debt is above target, deficits are still trimmed, but more gently. The burden falls on revenue spending, especially development expenditure, while capital expenditure stays protected.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 50-52; Vision IAS p. 62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the Union Budget 2026-27, total expenditure falls as a share of GDP more than proportionately to the fall in the deficit.
Statement-II: Non-debt receipts as a share of GDP are lower in FY27 (BE) than in FY26.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Non-debt receipts slip from 9.5 to 9.3 per cent of GDP, so cutting the deficit from 4.4 to 4.3 per cent requires a larger fall in spending, from 13.9 to 13.6 per cent. Capital expenditure stays at about 3.1 per cent, so revenue spending, particularly on development and rural employment, absorbs the squeeze.

questions.q:
With reference to Tax Collected at Source and the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. Tax Collected at Source is collected by buyers from sellers at the time of sale.
2. The Scheme permits remittances for lottery and speculative trading within the annual limit.
3. The Scheme is confined to capital account transactions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Sellers collect this tax from buyers, under Section 206C of the Income Tax Act, 1961; it is deduction at source that runs the other way. Gambling, lottery, trading and speculation are prohibited under the Scheme. Permitted remittances may be on current account, capital account or both. Budget 2026-27 cut the collection rate on education and medical expenses abroad.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 61-62; TDS contrast is static

questions.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is placed at 4.3 per cent of GDP and the primary deficit at 0.7 per cent of GDP for FY27. The gap of 3.6 percentage points between them represents which one of the following?
questions.e: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments, so the gap between the two shows the cost of servicing past debt. Revenue deficit is the shortfall on the revenue account, a different cut of the same borrowing. Capital expenditure, about 3.1 per cent of GDP, is a spending item, and non-debt capital receipts reduce the deficit rather than measure this gap.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 50-52; glossary 13.1; definitions are static

questions.q:
In the horizontal devolution formula of the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following pairs:
Criterion : Weight
1. Per capita GSDP distance : 42.5 per cent
2. Population : 17.5 per cent
3. Area : 15 per cent
4. Contribution to GDP : 2.5 per cent
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Area was cut from 15 to 10 per cent. Contribution to GDP, the new criterion, carries 10 per cent, and demographic performance and forest also get 10 per cent each. The lower area weight together with the GDP criterion appears to favour southern and industrialised States, while poorer States that rely on equity criteria lose some relative advantage.

questions.q:
With reference to Finance Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. The First Finance Commission was chaired by K.C. Neogy.
2. State Finance Commissions are constituted under Articles 243-I and 243-Y.
3. State Finance Commissions are set up by the Governor every five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The First Commission was constituted by Presidential Order on 22 November 1951. Article 243-I covers Panchayats and 243-Y covers Municipalities. Weak or delayed State Finance Commissions limit how far the Union Commission can reach the third tier, which is why the 16th Commission made timely constitution an entry condition for local body grants.

questions.q:
Among reforms supporting ease of doing business, consider the following pairs:
Reform : Fact
1. Business Reforms Action Plan : Run by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
2. Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 : Decriminalised provisions in Acts across several ministries
3. SPICe+ : Integrates systems of ministries for real-time cargo tracking
4. Unified Logistics Interface Platform : Merges company-incorporation procedures, including PAN, into one web form
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pairs 3 and 4 are interchanged: SPICe+ merges ten incorporation procedures, including DIN, PAN, TAN and GSTIN, while the logistics platform integrates over 35 systems for cargo tracking. The Action Plan dates from 2014. The Jan Vishwas Act covered 183 provisions in 42 Acts of 19 ministries and departments, reducing the criminal risk of minor lapses.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding business reform are correct?
1. B-READY is a successor index being developed by UNCTAD.
2. U-PIN is described as 'Aadhaar for Land'.
3. District-BRAP aims to move reform decisions from municipalities up to the Union government.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. B-READY is the World Bank's index, succeeding Doing Business, in which India ranked 63rd in the 2019 report, so statement 1 fails. District-BRAP runs the other way, carrying reforms from State capitals down to municipalities and equipping urban local bodies digitally for permits. The land parcel number aims at dispute-free digital titles, since land is a State subject.

questions.q: The 'Entrepreneurial State', a term invoked in the Economic Survey 2025-26, is associated with which one of the following economists?
questions.e: The term comes from Mariana Mazzucato, and the Survey ties it to strategic indispensability, or building capabilities others depend on. The barriers it identifies include officials being punished for action, irreversibility creep and retrospective scrutiny. Claudia Goldin is cited this month for the U-curve of women's work. Duflo and Stiglitz are well-known economists but are not linked with this concept.

questions.q: Which one of the following best explains why asset monetisation under the National Monetisation Pipeline is different from a sale of ownership?
o: Assets are transferred permanently to private owners at a discount to book value
Assets are moved to State governments to be run as public sector undertakings
Assets are converted into equity in an international sovereign wealth fund
Assets are leased or licensed for a fixed period under a concession, with proceeds recycled into new assets
questions.e: Monetisation leases or licenses public assets to private operators for a fixed period under a concession agreement, and ownership stays public. Proceeds go largely to the Consolidated Fund and are recycled into new assets, which is why it is also called capital recycling. The perception that it equals privatisation remains a challenge, alongside valuation problems and disputes that can deter investors.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Model)
A. Toll-Operate-Transfer
B. Rehabilitate-Operate-Maintain-Transfer
C. Infrastructure Investment Trust
List II (Feature)
1. Pools investor funds to invest directly in infrastructure
2. One-time lump sum paid for a long-term right to collect fees
3. Asset is upgraded before operation and revenue collection resume
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Toll-Operate-Transfer gives a private investor the right to collect fees on an operational highway for 15-30 years in exchange for a lump sum. The rehabilitation model adds upgrading before operations begin. Investment trusts are structured finance, working like mutual funds that hold infrastructure, whereas the first two are contractual concessions. Real Estate Investment Trusts do the same for real estate.

questions.q:
Regarding asset monetisation, consider the following statements:
1. National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 was built around greenfield infrastructure.
2. National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 achieved less than half of its Rs 6 lakh crore target.
3. Monetisation works by raising the fiscal deficit in the initial years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The first pipeline focused on brownfield assets, offering quicker and cheaper entry despite legacy limits. It achieved 89 per cent of its target over FY22 to FY25. Monetisation yields revenue from under-used public assets through private participation without raising the fiscal deficit. Railways met only 30 per cent of revised goals, showing uneven performance even though the overall pipeline did well.

questions.q:
With reference to National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It was prepared by NITI Aayog.
2. Highways, including multimodal logistics parks and ropeways, have the largest sectoral share.
3. Coal is excluded from its sectors.
4. It generally covers non-core assets such as government land, with core assets added only where development is planned.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Coal is included, at about 13 per cent, so statement 3 fails. Statement 4 reverses the principle: the pipeline focuses on core assets, with non-core land, buildings and real estate included only where further development is planned. The National Land Monetisation Corporation separately handles the non-core assets of central public enterprises. Highways account for 26 per cent.

questions.q:
With reference to the merchandise trade indices, consider the following statements:
1. Net barter terms of trade compare export prices with import prices.
2. Gross barter terms of trade compare the physical quantity of imports with that of exports.
3. Income terms of trade equal net terms of trade multiplied by export quantity.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The net measure asks what exports can buy in price terms. The gross measure compares volumes. The income measure captures purchasing power of total exports, so a fall in price can be offset by higher volume. The Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics compiles the merchandise trade indices used to measure these concepts.

questions.q:
Regarding Advance Pricing Agreements and related changes in Budget 2026-27, consider the following statements:
1. Such an agreement fixes in advance the transfer-pricing method for specified transactions.
2. Safe-harbour eligibility for IT services was reduced from Rs 2,000 crore to Rs 300 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the agreement gives certainty and reduces disputes over arm's-length pricing between related parties. Statement 2 reverses the numbers: the threshold rose from Rs 300 crore to Rs 2,000 crore, with IT services merged under a single category at a uniform margin. The process is to finish within two years, extendable by six months.

questions.q: The 'Smiling Curve' in global value chains indicates that:
o: value is highest at the assembly stage and falls at both ends
value rises steadily from raw material to retail without a dip
value is highest upstream in research and design and downstream in branding, and lowest in manufacturing
the share of labour income rises as countries move out of assembly
questions.e: The curve shows the highest value at the two ends, in R&D and design upstream and in branding and marketing downstream, with the lowest in the middle, in manufacturing and assembly. Budget 2026-27's two-track strategy aims to move India from low-value assembly towards design, R&D and components, part of the idea of strategic indispensability in global value chains.

questions.q:
As regards biologics, consider the following statements:
1. Biologics are produced from living or natural sources.
2. Biosimilars are highly similar copies of a reference biologic with no clinically meaningful differences.
3. Biopharmaceuticals are typically taken orally, unlike small-molecule drugs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: these medicines are usually given by injection or infusion, not orally, because they are large molecules made through biotechnology. Examples include vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, modern insulin and recombinant proteins. Biopharma SHAKTI aims to build domestic production of such products as the disease burden shifts to non-communicable diseases.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 38-40; Shankar IAS pp. 54-56

questions.q:
In the biotechnology and pharma policy space, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Associated fact
1. National Biopharma Mission : Co-funded by the World Bank and implemented by BIRAC
2. Bio-RIDE : A scheme of the Department of Pharmaceuticals for Bulk Drug Parks
3. PRIP : A research scheme of the Department of Biotechnology limited to vaccines
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Bio-RIDE, launched in September 2024, is about biotechnology research and entrepreneurship, covering industry-academia links and biomanufacturing, not Bulk Drug Parks. PRIP, from the Department of Pharmaceuticals in 2023, covers new drugs, biosimilars, complex generics, precision medicine and devices, with Centres of Excellence at the national pharmaceutical institutes. BIRAC itself sits under the Department of Biotechnology.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 38-40; Shankar IAS pp. 54-56

questions.q: The three Bulk Drug Parks sanctioned by the Government of India are located in:
o: Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh
questions.e: The parks are in Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, with an outlay of Rs 3,000 crore. They aim to reduce India's heavy dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients, mainly from China. Telangana, Maharashtra and other pharma-heavy States look plausible, since they have large pharmaceutical bases, but they are not the three chosen locations under this scheme.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 38-40; Shankar IAS pp. 54-56

questions.q:
In respect of India's pharmaceutical sector, consider the following statements:
1. FDI up to 100 per cent is allowed through the automatic route in greenfield pharma.
2. Evergreening refers to extending patent life through minor, non-essential modifications.
3. Price caps under the Drug Price Control Order are based on the National List of Essential Medicines.
4. FDI up to 100 per cent is allowed through the automatic route in brownfield pharma.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Brownfield pharma has automatic-route FDI only up to 74 per cent, while greenfield gets 100 per cent, so statement 4 fails. Evergreening and price controls are listed among sector challenges, with price caps said to squeeze margins and research. Dependence on imported active ingredients, mainly from China, is what Bulk Drug Parks address.

questions.q:
With reference to the Trade Receivables Discounting System, consider the following statements:
1. Only MSMEs can be sellers on it.
2. Corporates, government departments and public sector undertakings can be buyers.
3. Budget 2026-27 proposes that TReDS receivables can be traded in a secondary market as asset-backed securities.
4. CGTMSE guarantee cover for invoice discounting on it was announced.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. It lets MSMEs discount receivables from buyers through multiple financiers, including banks and NBFC-Factors. The Budget also made it mandatory for central public sector enterprises to settle purchases from MSMEs through this platform, and linked it with the Government e-Marketplace to share purchase data with financiers. These measures form the liquidity prong of the Champion MSME approach.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Very few registered MSMEs in India are medium enterprises.
Statement-II: Compliance costs encourage firms to stay small or informal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked; this is the missing middle. As of November 2023, about 97.92 per cent of registered units were micro and only 0.01 per cent medium. As firms grow, regulation and tax compliance become heavier, so staying small can be rational. Budget 2026-27 tries to help through equity, liquidity and Corporate Mitras, the accredited para-professionals for compliance.

questions.q:
Regarding support to small enterprises, consider the following pairs:
Scheme or provision : Feature
1. Public Procurement Policy for MSEs : 25 per cent annual procurement from micro and small enterprises
2. PM Vishwakarma : Support for artisans of 18 trades
3. RAMP : Asian Development Bank-supported Centrally Sponsored Scheme
4. MSME Champion Scheme : Components include ZED and LEAN
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. RAMP is World Bank-supported and a Central Sector Scheme, so pair 3 fails on both counts. The Champion Scheme has sustainable, competitive and innovative components. The procurement mandate binds Central Ministries, Departments and public enterprises. PM Vishwakarma, launched in 2023, gives end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople.

questions.q:
Under the MSMED Act, 2006, as amended, on which of the following are MSMEs classified?
1. Investment in plant, machinery or equipment
2. Annual turnover
3. Number of employees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Classification rests on investment and annual turnover, after the 2020 amendment. Land and building are left out of investment, and employee count is not a criterion. Budget 2025-26 raised the investment limits by 2.5 times and the turnover limits by two times, effective 1 April 2025. Many candidates wrongly assume a headcount test because the sector is described by employment.

questions.q: Which one of the following entities recognises a startup under the Startup India Action Plan?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Small Industries Development Bank of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.e: Recognition is given by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. SIDBI has a funding role and is often confused with the recognition authority, as is the MSME Ministry, whose domain differs. SEBI regulates venture capital funds but does not recognise startups. The revised framework adds a Deep Tech sub-category and cooperatives.

questions.q:
With reference to the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. Its capex incentive runs for a longer period than its turnover-linked incentive.
2. Its turnover-linked incentive allows an optional gestation year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is reversed: the turnover-linked incentive runs for six years, with one optional gestation year, and the capex incentive for five. There is also a hybrid route. These incentives target items such as display modules, camera sub-assemblies and multilayer printed circuit boards, because India is more assembly-oriented and imports much of its components.

questions.q:
Under India's electronics policy, consider the following statements:
1. SPECS offers a capex incentive.
2. The Semicon India Programme leaves chip design out of its incentives.
3. FDI in electronics manufacturing is capped at 74 per cent under the automatic route.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: SPECS gives 25 per cent on capital expenditure. The 2021 Semicon India Programme supports semiconductor and display fabs and includes a Design Linked Incentive, so statement 2 fails. FDI of 100 per cent is allowed through the automatic route, so statement 3 fails. Obstacles remain a cost gap of 10-20 per cent against China, Vietnam and Mexico.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's Second Five-Year Plan prioritised heavy and capital-goods industries.
Statement-II: The Mahalanobis model provided the basis of that Plan.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Both are correct and connected. The model argued that investing in capacity to make machines speeds long-run growth, which shaped the 1956-61 Plan. The theme returns because capital goods are still about 12 per cent of manufacturing output, around 40 per cent are imported, and the 2016 national policy's goal of 20 per cent by 2025 was not achieved.

questions.q:
With reference to the capital goods sector, consider the following statements:
1. The National Capital Goods Policy 2016 target for the sector's share in manufacturing was achieved ahead of 2025.
2. Budget 2026-27 gave non-residents supplying capital goods to toll manufacturers in bonded zones a five-year income-tax exemption.
3. India is a permanent member of the Washington Accord on engineering education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The goal of raising the share from 12 to 20 per cent by 2025 was not achieved, and a draft 2025 policy has followed. The tax exemption aims to bring in tooling for toll manufacturing. The Accord matters for engineers' mobility, and R&D in the sector, near 0.9 per cent, remains below the policy's 2.8 per cent aim.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Capital expenditure is the main casualty of spending compression in the Union Budget 2026-27.
Statement-II: Capital expenditure is generally credited with a high multiplier.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is wrong: capital expenditure stays about 3.1 per cent of GDP and rises about 9 per cent to Rs 12.2 lakh crore. Statement-II is right, and the high multiplier is the reason capital spending is protected. The squeeze falls instead on revenue spending, notably development expenditure and rural employment. Critics add that the corporate tax ratio remains around pre-Covid levels.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 50-52; Vision IAS pp. 55-57

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a sub-component of the Integrated Programme for the Textile Sector announced in the Union Budget 2026-27?
questions.e: Silk Samagra is a separate, existing initiative. The five sub-components are the National Fibre Scheme, the Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme, the National Handloom and Handicraft Programme, the Tex-Eco Initiative and Samarth 2.0. They address fibre self-reliance, cluster modernisation, artisan support, sustainability and skilling respectively. PM MITRA parks and Tex-RAMPS are also earlier initiatives outside this list.

questions.q:
On textile exports, consider the following statements:
1. Budget 2026-27 extended the export obligation period from 6 to 12 months for garment, footwear and leather exporters using duty-free imported inputs.
2. Kasturi Cotton Bharat is a branding initiative linked to cotton traceability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. A longer export obligation gives exporters more time to use inputs imported duty-free, easing their working-capital pressure. Traceability, also supported through the Kapas Kisan app, helps Indian cotton meet buyer standards in markets such as the EU. The sector faces competition from Bangladesh and Vietnam, with about 47 per cent of exports going to the USA and EU.

questions.q:
With reference to India's rare-earth and chemical-park initiatives, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Stated detail
1. Rare earth corridors in Budget 2026-27 : Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
2. Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Scheme : Rs 7,280 crore
3. Chemical Parks in Budget 2026-27 : Rs 600 crore for three parks
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three are correct. The corridors cover mining, processing, research and manufacturing of magnets. The magnet scheme supports a chain from rare-earth oxides to finished magnets, with 6,000 tonnes a year of capacity. The chemical parks are cluster-based and plug-and-play, addressing a chemical trade deficit and a focus on bulk rather than speciality products, with research spending only 0.7 per cent.

questions.q:
With reference to Rare Earth Permanent Magnets, consider the following statements:
1. During 2022-25, India imported most of them by quantity from Japan.
2. They are used in electric vehicle motors and wind turbine generators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 fails because China supplied 85-90 per cent of these magnets by quantity and 60-80 per cent by value during 2022-25, which is why dependence has become a strategic concern. Demand is expected to double by 2030, as the magnets also serve defence equipment and precision sensors, tying them to the clean-energy transition and to security.

questions.q: The expression 'Orange Economy' was popularised by a 2013 book written by:
o: Ivan Duque Marquez and Felipe Buitrago
questions.e: Ivan Duque Marquez, a former President of Colombia, and Felipe Buitrago, an ex-culture minister, coined it in their book. Orange was chosen for its links with culture, creativity and identity. Florida and Howkins are writers on creative industries, making them close distractors. The concept rests on goods and services whose value lies mainly in intellectual property.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 44-46; Florida and Howkins are static

questions.q:
On global creative-economy initiatives, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Link
1. Bridgetown Covenant : UNCTAD
2. Bali Agenda : WTO Ministerial Conference
3. International Year of Creative Economy for Sustainable Development : UNESCO General Conference
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. The Covenant places culture and creativity at the centre of trade, technology and diversification. The Bali Agenda of 2018 came from the World Conferences on Creative Economy, not the WTO. The UN General Assembly, not UNESCO, declared 2021 as the International Year. In India, the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies in Mumbai is the national centre of excellence.

questions.q: Claudia Goldin's U-curve of female labour force participation suggests that participation:
o: falls continuously as countries become richer
rises in early industrialisation and falls once services expand
falls in early industrialisation and rises when education crosses a threshold and services expand
rises steadily with income, without any fall
questions.e: The curve says women leave farm work in early industrialisation, as they lack factory skills or social permission, and return when education passes a threshold and services grow. Social norms, the parenthood effect and technology shape it. The Nobel laureate's framework is used to read India's data, as the Economic Survey says raising participation towards 55 per cent by 2050 may be key to growth.

questions.q:
With reference to women's employment provisions in India, consider the following statements:
1. Labour Codes provide 26 weeks of paid maternity leave, and 12 weeks for adoptive or commissioning mothers.
2. She-Box is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to register wage complaints.
3. SHE-Mart, from Budget 2026-27, provides markets for products of self-help groups and rural women.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. She-Box belongs to the Ministry of Women and Child Development and takes complaints under the POSH Act, 2013, so statement 2 fails. The Labour Codes also prohibit gender discrimination in wages and require creches. Unpaid work remains a binding constraint, with women spending 363 minutes a day compared with 123 minutes for men.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Fund or programme under DAY-NRLM : Purpose
1. Revolving Fund : Internal lending and immediate credit in self-help groups
2. Community Investment Fund : Creditworthiness and financial management
3. Viability Gap Fund : Covering operating costs until sustainability
4. Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana : Skilling of rural youth for urban transport jobs
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana gives subsidised loans for rural transport services; it is not a skilling scheme, so pair 4 fails. These instruments support the Lakhpati Didi initiative. Self-help group members are identified through two or more years' membership and use of the Community Investment Fund, with at least two livelihood activities.

questions.q: A 'Lakhpati Didi' is defined by which one of the following conditions?
o: A woman entrepreneur who has received a loan of Rs 1 lakh under the Mudra scheme
A rural woman whose individual annual savings exceed Rs 1 lakh in a Jan-Dhan account
A self-help group whose annual turnover exceeds Rs 1 lakh for one financial year
A self-help group member with annual household income above Rs 1 lakh, sustained for four agricultural seasons or business cycles
questions.e: It requires annual household income above Rs 1,00,000 at an average of Rs 10,000 a month across four agricultural seasons or business cycles. It is an income measure for a self-help group member's household, not a loan, savings or group-turnover test. The initiative began in 2023 under DAY-NRLM in the Ministry of Rural Development, and the target now stands at six crore by March 2029.

questions.q:
With reference to the origin and spread of rice, consider the following statements:
1. Recent archaeology confirms that rice originated only in China.
2. India has close to half of the rice varieties known globally.
3. India's broken rice goes to China for animal feed and ethanol.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Archaeology suggesting domestication as early as the Indus Valley Civilisation challenges the China-only view, pointing to parallel domestication, so statement 1 fails. India has about 60,000 of some 1,23,000 known varieties, though post-Green Revolution policy favoured a few high-yielding ones. Basmati, by contrast, goes mainly to the Middle East, Europe and the USA.

questions.q:
With reference to the Preservation of Subsoil Water Act, 2009, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Stubble burning in north India worsened as an unintended outcome of the Act.
Statement-II: Delayed paddy transplanting narrowed the window between rice harvest and the next sowing.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and connected. The Punjab and Haryana law postpones transplanting so that irrigation shifts from groundwater to the monsoon. The later harvest leaves less time before the next crop, and farmers clear fields by burning stubble, adding to seasonal air pollution. The case shows how a sound groundwater measure can cause harm elsewhere, a classic policy trade-off.

questions.q:
On India's rice economy, consider the following statements:
1. India's central pool rice stock on 1 January 2026 was well above the buffer norm.
2. India's yield per hectare is higher than China's.
3. Non-basmati rice has a larger share of export volume than of export value.
4. Oryza sativa indica developed in a setting where rice was grown only in winter.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Stocks of 63.06 million tonnes far exceeded the 7.61 million tonne norm. China's yield of about 7,100 kg per hectare is much above India's 2,929, so statement 2 fails. Non-basmati is about 70 per cent of volume and 48 per cent of value. In the Indus Valley, rice was grown in both summer and winter.

questions.q:
In the law and policy on food security, consider the following statements:
1. The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to 75 per cent of the rural and 50 per cent of the urban population.
2. Nationwide roll-out of rice fortification was approved by the Cabinet in 2022, after pilots from 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Act covers about two-thirds of the population, roughly 81.35 crore beneficiaries, through the Targeted Public Distribution System. Fortified rice adds iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 to address anaemia. Rice accounts for over 65 per cent of foodgrains distributed, which is why the pool remains central to welfare even as water concerns over paddy grow.

questions.q:
On storage and crop diversification, consider the following pairs:
Committee or audit : Recommendation
1. Shanta Kumar Committee : Convert old Food Corporation of India storage to silos and expand Negotiable Warehouse Receipts
2. CAG Performance Audit (2023) : Phase out Covered and Plinth storage
3. Ashok Dalwai Committee : Storage based on Primary Agricultural Credit Societies
4. S.S. Johl Committee : Diversify part of Punjab's cropped area
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are correct. Shanta Kumar's 2014 panel also sought real-time computerised stock tracking. The CAG wants capacity planned under the national storage policy completed. Dalwai's 2018 panel on doubling farmers' income backed decentralised storage at society level. Johl's 1986 panel asked for at least 20 per cent diversification, a concern that Punjab's 2025 maize pilot revisits.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 59-61; Shankar IAS pp. 3-5

questions.q:
Which of the following statements on agricultural infrastructure are correct?
1. Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure is a component of PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana.
2. The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund dates from 2020.
3. The grain storage plan in the cooperative sector works through convergence of existing schemes at the level of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure is a component of the Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing, not of SAMPADA, which concerns food-processing infrastructure from farm gate to retail. The Fund finances warehouses, cold storage and logistics, and its credit target is being doubled. Convergence is needed because 60-70 per cent of grain is stored in vulnerable household structures.

questions.q: With reference to the regulation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Multi-State societies : Entry 44 of the Union List
Single-State societies : Entry 44 of the Union List
Single-State societies : Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies
Multi-State societies : Entry 32 of the State List
questions.e: Multi-State bodies come under Entry 44 of the Union List and are administered by the Central Registrar under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. Single-State societies fall under Entry 32 of the State List and are handled by State Registrars. The 2023 amendment mandates board representation for women and SC/ST members, and Model Bye-laws make these societies multipurpose.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the main mission promoting location-specific Integrated Farming System clusters?
o: Rainfed Area Development under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture
questions.e: Rainfed Area Development is the main mission for clusters. RKVY gives States flexible funding, Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana supports organic nutrient cycling, and the Abhiyan is a lab-to-land outreach by scientists. Each has a part in the model, which is relevant because about 89.4 per cent of farmers hold under 2 hectares and benefit from diversified income on one farm.

questions.q:
In India's civil aviation sector, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A disruption at the largest airline in India shrinks total capacity rather than shifting passengers to others.
Statement-II: IndiGo is the sole carrier on a majority of routes.
Statement-III: Flight Duty Time Limitation norms apply only to foreign crew.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-II is correct: IndiGo is the only carrier on about 60.4 per cent of routes, and with the Air India group it holds about 90 per cent of domestic traffic. That explains Statement-I. Statement-III is wrong: the norms bind Indian operations, and breaches appeared in DGCA safety-violation notices. Carriers abroad keep 20-25 per cent spare crew.

questions.q:
As reported in February 2026, consider the following statements on Indian aviation:
1. India is the world's largest domestic aviation market.
2. FDI in greenfield airports is capped at 49 per cent.
3. Technical posts sanctioned for the Directorate General of Civil Aviation are almost fully staffed.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. India is the third-largest domestic market. FDI is permitted up to 100 per cent in greenfield and 74 per cent in brownfield projects. Nearly half of the regulator's sanctioned technical posts are vacant, and crises tend to be handled by schedule exemptions rather than enforcement. Pilot supply is also inelastic, as training is costly and simulators are short.

questions.q:
With reference to Namo Bharat RRTS, consider the following statements:
1. It is implemented by a joint venture of the Centre with Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi.
2. It runs on tracks shared with conventional long-distance passenger trains.
3. It has more frequent stops than a Metro.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct, describing the National Capital Region Transport Corporation. The system uses a dedicated corridor, so statement 2 fails. Compared with a Metro, it covers longer distances with fewer stops at higher speed, up to 180 km per hour, so statement 3 also fails. The Delhi-Meerut line cuts travel from about three hours to 60 minutes.
